questions.question: Which of the following services have been integrated into the newly revamped Mission Vatsalya Portal launched by the Ministry of Women and Child Development in July 2025?

options.text: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao and Childline 1098
Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana and Sakhi

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**TrackChild and Khoya-Paya Services**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mission Vatsalya Portal** is a comprehensive platform launched by the **Ministry of Women and Child Development** to protect and rehabilitate children in need of care and protection.
 
• In **July 2025**, the newly revamped portal integrated several services, including **TrackChild** and **Khoya-Paya**, which are key tools for tracking missing children and ensuring their safety.
 
• **TrackChild**: This initiative is a nationwide tracking system that helps in locating missing children and linking them with their families or providing them institutional care.
 
• **Khoya-Paya Services**: This is an online citizen-based platform to report and track missing and found children, encouraging public participation in child welfare.
 
• Other schemes like **Poshan Abhiyaan**, **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao**, and **Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana** are critical government initiatives, but they are not directly integrated into the Mission Vatsalya Portal. *Hence, options 1, 2, and 4 are incorrect.*
 
• The integration of **TrackChild** and **Khoya-Paya** services aligns with the mission's objective of ensuring a safe environment for children and expediting their rehabilitation. *Hence, option 3 is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **TrackChild:**

 
 
• It is an initiative by the **Ministry of Women and Child Development** in partnership with the **Ministry of Home Affairs**.
 
• The platform connects stakeholders, including police, child welfare committees, and childcare institutions, to trace missing children.
 
• It features a centralized database of missing and found children, accessible to law enforcement agencies and authorized officials.
 
• Parents and guardians can also register complaints and track updates about their missing children.
 
 
 
• **Khoya-Paya Services:**
 
 
• Launched in **2015** by the Government of India, this citizen-centric platform enables people to report missing or found children.
 
• It serves as a bridge between the public and government authorities, accelerating the process of locating children.
 
• The platform uses technology to disseminate information quickly, increasing the chances of reuniting children with their families.
 
• It complements the **TrackChild** initiative by mobilizing community support for child welfare.
 
 
 
• **Mission Vatsalya:**
 
 
• This is an umbrella scheme aimed at **child protection, welfare, and development**, focusing on children in difficult circumstances.
 
• It emphasizes strengthening the child protection system, institutional care, and non-institutional care, such as adoption and foster care.
 
• The program also promotes awareness and participation among stakeholders and communities to safeguard children's rights.
 
 
 
• **Other Integrated Child Protection Services (ICPS):**
 
 
• ICPS was merged into Mission Vatsalya to create a unified framework for child protection in India.
 
• It includes services like open shelters, child helplines, and sponsorships to aid vulnerable children.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Childline 1098:** This is a toll-free helpline service for children in distress, operational under the Mission Vatsalya framework.
 
• **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao:** This scheme focuses on gender equality and improving the survival and education of the girl child, but it is not directly integrated into the portal.
 
• **Poshan Abhiyaan:** It addresses malnutrition and is aimed at improving the nutritional outcomes for children and women but operates independently of Mission Vatsalya.
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana:** A maternity benefit program for pregnant women and lactating mothers, providing conditional cash transfers, but it is separate from the Mission Vatsalya Portal's scope.

questions.question: In June 2025, the Bonn Climate Change Conference 2025 was held in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Germany**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bonn Climate Change Conference 2025** was held in **Bonn, Germany**, which has historically been a hub for United Nations climate-related activities.
 
• **Bonn** serves as the headquarters of the **United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)**, making it a significant venue for hosting climate conferences.
 
• The conference aims to advance global climate negotiations, review progress on commitments made under the **Paris Agreement**, and strengthen international cooperation to combat climate change.
 
• Participants at the Bonn Climate Change Conference include representatives from **government bodies, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), scientists, and policymakers**, who discuss strategies for achieving sustainable development and reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• Bonn has hosted multiple climate conferences in the past, including the annual meetings of the **Subsidiary Bodies** to the UNFCCC, which focus on technical and implementation issues related to climate action.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC):**

 
 
• The **UNFCCC** was established in **1992** at the Earth Summit held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, to address global climate change.
 
• Its primary objective is to stabilize greenhouse gas concentrations in the atmosphere at a level that prevents dangerous anthropogenic interference with the climate system.
 
• Key agreements under the UNFCCC include the **Kyoto Protocol (1997)** and the **Paris Agreement (2015)**.
 
• The UNFCCC Secretariat is based in **Bonn, Germany**, making the city a focal point for international climate negotiations.
 
 
 
• **Paris Agreement:**
 
 
• Adopted in **2015**, the Paris Agreement aims to limit global warming to well below **2°C**, preferably to **1.5°C**, above pre-industrial levels.
 
• Countries under the agreement are required to submit **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)**, outlining their plans to reduce emissions and adapt to climate change.
 
• The agreement emphasizes global cooperation, capacity-building, and financial support for developing countries to achieve their climate goals.
 
 
 
• **Bonn's Role in Climate Diplomacy:**
 
 
• Bonn is home to several UN organizations, including the Secretariat of the UNFCCC, making it a hub for international climate diplomacy.
 
• The city hosts regular meetings of the Subsidiary Bodies to the UNFCCC, which focus on implementing policies and technical measures related to climate change.
 
• Bonn also serves as a venue for preparatory meetings ahead of the annual **Conference of Parties (COP)**, where major climate decisions are made.
 
 
 
• **Important Conferences in Bonn:**
 
 
• The **Bonn Climate Change Conference** is part of the mid-year sessions of the UNFCCC, held annually to track progress on climate commitments and prepare for the COP.
 
• Previous Bonn conferences have played a crucial role in shaping global climate policies and advancing negotiations under the Paris Agreement.
 
• In **2017**, Bonn hosted the **23rd Conference of Parties (COP23)**, chaired by Fiji, which focused on implementation guidelines for the Paris Agreement.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Germany's commitment to climate action:**

 
 
• Germany is a leading advocate for international climate action and has implemented ambitious policies to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• The country aims to achieve **climate neutrality by 2045**, ahead of the EU's target of 2050.
 
• Germany's **Energiewende (Energy Transition)** focuses on phasing out fossil fuels and increasing reliance on renewable energy sources like wind and solar power.
 
 
 
• **Subsidiary Bodies to the UNFCCC:**
 
 
• The Subsidiary Body for Scientific and Technological Advice (**SBSTA**) and the Subsidiary Body for Implementation (**SBI**) are key components of the UNFCCC process.
 
• SBSTA provides scientific and technical advice, while SBI focuses on implementing climate policies and reviewing progress.
 
• Both bodies meet in Bonn to advance technical discussions and prepare for the COP.
 
 
 
• **Global Climate Goals:**
 
 
• The **Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC)** highlights the urgent need to limit global warming to **1.5°C** to prevent severe climate impacts.
 
• Achieving this goal requires rapid and deep reductions in greenhouse gas emissions across all sectors.
 
• International cooperation, technology transfer, and financial support are critical for achieving climate goals, especially in developing countries.

questions.question: In 2025, which Union Minister inaugurated the Khelo India multipurpose hall in Kamle district, Arunachal Pradesh?

questions.question: Which Pakistani female cricketer was inducted into the ICC Hall of Fame in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sana Mir**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sana Mir**, a former captain of the Pakistan women's cricket team, was inducted into the **ICC Hall of Fame** in **June 2025**. This is a prestigious recognition of her contributions to cricket at the global level.
 
• She is widely acknowledged as one of the **greatest female cricketers** to emerge from Pakistan. Her leadership and performances have significantly shaped the growth of women's cricket in her country.
 
• Sana Mir has played an instrumental role in **leading Pakistan** to numerous achievements, including their first-ever **gold medals** in cricket at the Asian Games in **2010** and **2014**.
 
• In her illustrious career, she represented Pakistan in **120 ODIs** and **106 T20Is**, taking a total of 151 wickets in ODIs and 89 wickets in T20Is, alongside scoring crucial runs.
 
• Sana Mir retired from international cricket in **April 2020**, leaving behind a legacy that inspired many young girls in Pakistan to take up the sport.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **ICC Hall of Fame:**

 
 
• The **ICC Hall of Fame** was established in **2009** by the International Cricket Council (ICC) to honor legendary cricketers for their exceptional contributions to the game.
 
• Inductees are selected based on their **achievements, impact, and influence** on cricket over their careers.
 
• Previous inductees include legends such as **Sir Donald Bradman**, **Muttiah Muralitharan**, and **Jacques Kallis**.
 
 
 
• **Achievements of Sana Mir:**
 
 
• Sana Mir was the **first Pakistani woman** to take 100 wickets in ODIs, making her one of the top bowlers in women’s cricket.
 
• She was ranked as the **number one ODI bowler** in the ICC Women’s Rankings in **October 2018**.
 
• Under her captaincy, Pakistan won their **first-ever ODI series** against the West Indies in **2015**.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Explained:**
 
 
• **Diana Baig:** A talented Pakistani cricketer known for her pace bowling, but she has not been inducted into the ICC Hall of Fame.
 
• **Nida Dar:** A renowned all-rounder nicknamed "Lady Boom Boom," she is one of Pakistan’s best players but has not received this honor yet.
 
• **Bismah Maroof:** The current captain of the Pakistan women’s cricket team, known for her batting prowess, but she has not been inducted into the ICC Hall of Fame.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Sana Mir’s Induction:**
 
 
• Sana Mir’s recognition in the ICC Hall of Fame brings international attention to **women’s cricket in Pakistan**.
 
• It serves as an inspiration for young female cricketers in Pakistan and around the world to pursue the sport professionally.
 
• Her inclusion highlights the growing importance of **gender inclusivity** in global cricket.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The ICC Hall of Fame is a significant platform to honor players who have made exemplary contributions to the game.
 
• Sana Mir is a role model for aspiring cricketers, especially in countries where women’s sports face social and cultural barriers.
 
• Her achievements demonstrate the potential of women in cricket and emphasize the need for equal opportunities in sports globally.
 
• This milestone coincides with the increasing focus on promoting **women’s cricket** by the ICC and cricket boards worldwide.

questions.question: World Ocean Day 2025, observed on 8 June, emphasised which of the following themes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wonder: Sustaining what sustains us**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **World Ocean Day** is celebrated annually on **8 June** to raise awareness about the importance of oceans in maintaining ecological balance and promoting sustainable development.
 
• The theme for **World Ocean Day 2025** is **“Wonder: Sustaining what sustains us”**__, emphasizing the vital role oceans play in sustaining life on Earth and the urgent need to preserve them.
 
• This theme highlights the interconnectedness of human well-being and ocean health, encouraging global citizens to adopt sustainable practices and protect marine biodiversity.
 
• It calls for collective efforts by governments, organizations, and individuals to combat challenges like **ocean pollution, overfishing, and climate change.**
 
• World Ocean Day serves as a platform to promote ocean conservation initiatives, advocate for climate-resilient policies, and inspire action to protect marine ecosystems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Significance of the Theme:**

 
 
• The theme “Wonder: Sustaining what sustains us” focuses on fostering a sense of awe for the oceans and recognizing their critical importance in sustaining all forms of life.
 
• The oceans cover over **70% of the Earth’s surface**, regulate the planet’s climate, and provide oxygen, food, and livelihoods for billions of people.
 
• It emphasizes the need to balance human activities with the preservation of marine resources to ensure their long-term viability.
 
 
 
• **Challenges Facing the Oceans:**
 
 
• **Plastic Pollution:** Every year, approximately **8 million tons of plastic** enter the oceans, threatening marine life and ecosystems.
 
• **Overfishing:** Unsustainable fishing practices have led to the depletion of fish stocks, disrupting marine food chains.
 
• **Climate Change:** Rising sea temperatures and ocean acidification due to increased CO2 emissions are causing coral bleaching and biodiversity loss.
 
• **Habitat Destruction:** Activities like coastal development and bottom trawling damage critical marine habitats such as coral reefs and seagrass beds.
 
 
 
• **Global Initiatives for Ocean Conservation:**
 
 
• **United Nations Decade of Ocean Science for Sustainable Development (2021–2030):** Aims to enhance ocean science and promote sustainable management of marine resources.
 
• **Marine Protected Areas (MPAs):** Designated regions in oceans where human activity is regulated to conserve marine biodiversity.
 
• **Global Treaty on Marine Biodiversity:** Negotiated under the UN to protect biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction.
 
 
 
• **How Individuals Can Contribute:**
 
 
• Reduce the use of single-use plastics and participate in beach clean-up drives to minimize ocean pollution.
 
• Support sustainable seafood choices and avoid consuming overexploited species.
 
• Raise awareness about ocean conservation through social media and community initiatives.
 
• Advocate for policies that address climate change and protect marine ecosystems.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Background:**

 
 
• World Ocean Day was first proposed in **1992** at the Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, as a way to celebrate and protect the oceans.
 
• In **2008**, the United Nations officially recognized 8 June as World Ocean Day.
 
 
 
• **Economic Importance of Oceans:**
 
 
• The oceans contribute an estimated **$2.5 trillion annually** to the global economy, supporting industries like fisheries, tourism, and shipping.
 
• More than **3 billion people** rely on marine and coastal biodiversity for their livelihoods.

questions.question: Who among the following was appointed as a Whole-time Member (Life) at the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) in March 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swaminathan S Iyer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **March 2025**, **Swaminathan S Iyer** was appointed as a **Whole-time Member (Life)** at the **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)**.
 
• **IRDAI** is the statutory body established under the **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999**, tasked with regulating and promoting the insurance industry in India.
 
• Whole-time Members at IRDAI are responsible for ensuring the effective implementation of policies and guidelines aimed at improving the insurance sector.
 
• **Swaminathan S Iyer** has extensive experience in the insurance domain and regulatory frameworks, making him a suitable candidate for this role.
 
• The appointment of Whole-time Members at IRDAI is usually approved by the **Government of India**, following strict scrutiny of professional qualifications and contributions to the field.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI):**

 
 
• IRDAI was established in **2000** under the **IRDA Act, 1999**, with its headquarters in **Hyderabad, Telangana**.
 
• It is responsible for regulating the insurance industry to protect policyholders and ensure the growth of the insurance market.
 
• The authority also oversees the functioning of insurance companies, intermediaries, and agents to maintain transparency and accountability in the sector.
 
• **Key functions:** Licensing insurers, promoting consumer protection, regulating premium rates, and enforcing regulatory compliance in the insurance industry.
 
 
 
• **Role of Whole-time Members at IRDAI:**
 
 
• Whole-time Members are appointed to oversee specific domains within IRDAI, such as life insurance, general insurance, or health insurance.
 
• They ensure adherence to policies and formulate strategies for the effective regulation of insurance practices.
 
• These members play a crucial role in addressing grievances, implementing new policies, and promoting innovation in the insurance industry.
 
 
 
• **Other Relevant Appointments in IRDAI:**
 
 
• IRDAI consists of a **Chairperson**, **Whole-time Members**, and **Part-time Members**, all appointed by the **Government of India**.
 
• Appointments to IRDAI are made based on experience and expertise in insurance, financial regulation, law, or administration.
 
• Past appointments have included individuals with extensive contributions to the banking and insurance sectors.
 
 
 
• **Insurance Sector in India:**
 
 
• The insurance industry in India is one of the fastest-growing sectors, with approximately **57 insurance companies**, including **24 life insurers** and **33 non-life insurers**.
 
• IRDAI plays a pivotal role in supporting the government's initiatives such as **PMJJBY**, **PMSBY**, and **Ayushman Bharat**, aimed at increasing insurance penetration.
 
• India's insurance penetration was recorded at **4.2% in 2021**, highlighting the need for regulatory efforts to improve accessibility.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Appointment Process:**

 
 
• Appointments to statutory bodies like IRDAI are conducted through a rigorous selection process, ensuring candidates have relevant expertise and experience.
 
• Whole-time Members serve for a fixed term, usually **5 years**, or until the age of **62 years**, whichever is earlier.
 
• Their contributions significantly impact the regulation and growth of the insurance industry in India.
 
 
 
• **Insurance Penetration:**
 
 
• Insurance penetration refers to the ratio of premium underwritten to the GDP of a country.
 
• India's efforts to improve insurance penetration include initiatives like **PMJJBY** and **PMSBY**, which cater to marginalized sections of society.
 
• Regulatory measures by IRDAI aim to make insurance more accessible and affordable for all citizens.

questions.question: Where was India’s first wooden Gurdwara, Sri Nanak Niwas, constructed in Punjab in July 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fazilka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **first wooden Gurdwara** in India, Sri Nanak Niwas, was constructed in **Fazilka**, Punjab, in **July 2025**.
 
• The initiative is a significant step in promoting **eco-friendly architecture** and preserving cultural heritage in India.
 
• Fazilka is a border district in Punjab and holds immense historical significance due to its **proximity to the India-Pakistan border**.
 
• Wooden Gurdwaras are rare in India due to traditional construction practices; this project stands out as a **unique blend of traditional Sikh architecture and sustainable materials**.
 
• This Gurdwara is dedicated to the teachings of **Guru Nanak Dev Ji**, the founder of Sikhism, and aims to attract devotees and tourists alike.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Significance of Fazilka:**

 
 
• Fazilka is known for its **rich cultural and historical importance** in Punjab.
 
• The district is famous for its **heritage buildings, traditional bazaars, and agricultural practices**.
 
• It serves as a key location for **cross-border trade and cultural exchanges** with Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Architecture of Sri Nanak Niwas:**
 
 
• The Gurdwara is constructed using **sustainable wood**, which minimizes environmental impact compared to conventional construction materials.
 
• The design incorporates elements of **traditional Sikh architecture**, such as domes, arches, and intricate carvings.
 
• It also includes facilities for **community gatherings**, such as a langar hall and prayer rooms.
 
 
 
• **Eco-Friendly Construction:**
 
 
• Wooden structures are known for their **natural insulation properties**, which help in maintaining a comfortable indoor environment.
 
• The construction aligns with global trends of adopting **sustainable and renewable resources** in architecture.
 
• Wood is a **carbon-neutral material**, making it an environmentally friendly choice.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Wooden Gurdwaras:**
 
 
• Such structures symbolize a **return to traditional and natural construction practices**.

questions.question: In July 2025, which investigative authority unearthed over ₹24 crore in unaccounted assets in Karnataka?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka Lokayukta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Karnataka Lokayukta** is an independent anti-corruption ombudsman and investigative authority in the state of Karnataka, India.
 
• In **July 2025**, the Karnataka Lokayukta uncovered **over ₹24 crore** in unaccounted assets in a high-profile corruption case in Karnataka.
 
• The Lokayukta conducted **search and seizure operations** at various locations associated with government officials and private entities, leading to the revelation of these unaccounted assets.
 
• The investigation involved tracking financial irregularities, disproportionate assets, and suspected misuse of public office, which are core areas of Lokayukta’s jurisdiction.
 
• This operation underscores the **role of the Karnataka Lokayukta** in combating corruption and ensuring accountability in public administration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Karnataka Lokayukta:**

 
 
• Established under the Karnataka Lokayukta Act, 1984, it is one of the pioneering anti-corruption bodies in India.
 
• It is empowered to investigate allegations of corruption, misuse of power, and maladministration against public servants, including elected representatives, government officials, and private entities involved in public dealings.
 
• The Lokayukta operates independently of the state government, ensuring an unbiased investigation process.
 
• The Lokayukta’s findings and recommendations hold significant weight, often leading to disciplinary or legal action.
 
 
 
• **Other Investigative Authorities:**
 
 
• **Income Tax Department:** This authority investigates tax evasion, monitors financial transactions, and ensures compliance with income tax laws. However, it primarily focuses on tax-related offenses, not broader corruption cases.
 
• **Enforcement Directorate (ED):** The ED enforces laws related to money laundering and foreign exchange violations under FEMA and PMLA. It investigates financial crimes but does not directly deal with public administration corruption.
 
• **Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI):** The CBI investigates cases of corruption, economic offenses, and special crimes across India. However, state-level investigations like this one often fall under the jurisdiction of Lokayuktas or state-specific bodies.
 
 
 
• **Disproportionate Assets Cases:**
 
 
• These cases involve public officials possessing wealth that significantly exceeds their known sources of income.
 
• Such investigations require collaboration between multiple agencies, including Lokayuktas, tax departments, and forensic auditors.
 
• Unaccounted assets often include cash, gold, property, and other investments.
 
 
 
• **Anti-Corruption Efforts in India:**
 
 
• India has multiple anti-corruption bodies, including the **Central Vigilance Commission (CVC)**, Lokayuktas, and the CBI, to combat corruption at various levels.
 
• The **Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988**, is the primary legislation dealing with corruption in public offices.
 
• Recent amendments and stricter enforcement mechanisms aim to improve transparency and accountability in governance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Characteristics of Lokayuktas:**

 
 
• Lokayuktas are state-level anti-corruption bodies that complement the role of the Central Vigilance Commission at the national level.
 
• They investigate complaints from the public regarding corruption, abuse of power, or maladministration in state government offices.
 
• Lokayuktas have the authority to investigate even high-ranking officials, including the Chief Minister, in some states.
 
 
 
• **Significant Cases Handled by Lokayuktas:**
 
 
• In Karnataka, the Lokayukta has previously investigated several high-profile cases, including illegal mining scandals and disproportionate assets cases involving prominent politicians.
 
• Its proactive role has set benchmarks for anti-corruption efforts in other states.

questions.question: How much carbon sink does the Revised Green India Mission (GIM) Plan released in 2025 aim to create by 2030?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3.39 billion tonnes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Revised Green India Mission (GIM) Plan**, released in **2025**, aims to create a **carbon sink of 3.39 billion tonnes** by **2030**.
 
• The Green India Mission is one of the **eight national missions** under the **National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)** launched by the Government of India in **2010**.
 
• This mission focuses on **afforestation, reforestation, and ecosystem restoration** to enhance carbon sequestration and mitigate climate change.
 
• The target of **3.39 billion tonnes** aligns with India's commitments under the **Paris Agreement** to reduce **greenhouse gas emissions** and increase forest and tree cover.
 
• The mission emphasizes the involvement of local communities, especially in rural areas, to ensure sustainable development and environmental conservation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Green India Mission (GIM):**

 
 
• The Green India Mission was launched as part of India's response to **climate change adaptation and mitigation**.
 
• It aims to increase **forest/tree cover by 5 million hectares** and improve the quality of existing forest cover on **5 million hectares**.
 
• The mission includes activities like **ecosystem restoration, biodiversity conservation, and livelihood enhancement** for forest-dependent communities.
 
 
 
• **Carbon Sink:**
 
 
• A **carbon sink** refers to any system that absorbs more carbon dioxide than it emits. Examples include **forests, oceans, and soil**.
 
• By increasing forest cover and improving vegetation, the Green India Mission contributes to enhancing India's **natural carbon sinks**.
 
• This process helps in reducing the concentration of **CO2** in the atmosphere, thereby combating global warming.
 
 
 
• **Paris Agreement:**
 
 
• India is a signatory to the **Paris Agreement**, adopted in **2015**, which seeks to limit global temperature rise to **below 2°C**.
 
• Under its **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)**, India has committed to increasing its forest cover to help mitigate climate change.
 
 
 
• **Community Participation:**
 
 
• The Green India Mission encourages the active involvement of **local communities, panchayats, and NGOs** in afforestation and conservation projects.
 
• These efforts contribute to **sustainable rural development**, providing livelihoods to forest-dependent populations while ensuring ecological balance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Afforestation Targets:** The Green India Mission sets specific targets for **afforestation** and **reforestation** projects to enhance carbon sequestration.
 
• **Ecosystem Services:** The mission aims to improve **ecosystem services**, including water conservation, soil fertility, and biodiversity preservation.
 
• **Monitoring Mechanisms:** Advanced technologies like **GIS mapping** and remote sensing are employed to monitor progress and ensure accountability.
 
• **Climate Resilience:** The initiative also focuses on building **climate-resilient ecosystems** to minimize the adverse effects of climate change.
 
• **Budget Allocation:** Significant financial resources are allocated to achieve the mission's objectives effectively, with the support of **state governments and international organizations**.

questions.question: As of April 2025, which Ministry/Department approved 10 Plastic Parks in different states under the Scheme for Setting up of Plastic Parks in India?

options.text: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

questions.solution:

__
 
• The **Department of Chemicals and Petro-Chemicals** under the **Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers** is responsible for formulating and implementing policies related to the chemical and petrochemical industry in India.
 
• The **Scheme for Setting up of Plastic Parks in India** aims to establish dedicated zones for plastic manufacturing and allied industries to improve infrastructure and boost domestic production.
 
• As of **April 2025**, the Department has approved the development of **10 Plastic Parks** in various states, such as Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, and Jharkhand, among others.
 
• The main objectives of these parks include promoting a cluster-based approach for the plastic industry, increasing competitiveness, and reducing environmental impact through proper waste management systems.
 
• The scheme encourages public-private partnerships (PPP) and provides financial assistance of up to **50% of the project cost**, subject to a ceiling of **Rs. 40 crore per project**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• The scheme was launched in **2013** by the Department of Chemicals and Petro-Chemicals to create state-of-the-art infrastructure for the plastic industry.
 
• Each Plastic Park spans an area of around **100 to 150 acres** and includes facilities like testing labs, training centers, and recycling units.
 
• The scheme aims to attract investments in the plastic sector and generate **employment opportunities**, especially in rural and semi-urban areas.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Department of Chemicals and Petro-Chemicals:**
 
 
• It is responsible for the development of the chemical and petrochemical sectors, which are crucial for industrial and economic growth.
 
• Key initiatives include the promotion of green chemistry, reduction of plastic waste, and support for the "Make in India" campaign in the chemical and plastic sectors.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Benefits:**
 
 
• Plastic Parks aim to minimize the **environmental impact** of plastic production by incorporating modern waste management techniques.
 
• Recycling units in these parks help reduce plastic waste and promote the circular economy.
 
 
 
• **Other Relevant Ministries:**
 
 
• The **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change** is involved in regulating environmental standards for plastic manufacturing and waste management.
 
• The **Department of Pharmaceuticals** oversees the use of plastics in medical and pharmaceutical applications, ensuring compliance with safety standards.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• India is the third-largest producer of plastic in the world, with the industry contributing significantly to the economy.
 
• The plastic industry supports various sectors such as packaging, healthcare, automotive, and construction.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Plastic Management:**
 
 
• India generates approximately **3.5 million tonnes** of plastic waste annually, with a low recycling rate of around **60%**.
 
• The Plastic Parks Scheme is a step towards addressing these challenges by promoting sustainable practices and advanced technologies.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• Globally, countries like Germany and China have implemented similar industrial parks to support their plastic industries.
 
• India’s initiative aligns with international efforts to promote sustainable industrial growth and reduce plastic pollution.

questions.question: In June 2025, the Government of India launched which of the following new disaster management tech platforms?

options.text: Integrated Centre Room for Emergency Response
Integrated Control Room for Emergency Response
Integrated Common Response for Emergency Response
Indian Control Room for Emergency Response

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Integrated Control Room for Emergency Response**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Integrated Control Room for Emergency Response (ICR-ER)** was launched by the **Government of India** in **June 2025** to enhance disaster management capabilities and provide a centralized platform for monitoring and responding to emergencies effectively.
 
• The ICR-ER is equipped with **state-of-the-art technology** such as advanced predictive analytics, GIS mapping, and real-time data integration to handle emergencies like **natural disasters, industrial accidents, and public health crises**.
 
• This platform aims to **coordinate disaster response efforts** across various government departments, ensuring rapid deployment of resources to affected areas.
 
• The ICR-ER also integrates data from multiple sources, including **satellite imagery, weather forecasting systems, and local disaster management authorities**, to provide comprehensive situational awareness.
 
• The initiative is a part of India's broader efforts to strengthen its disaster management infrastructure under frameworks like the **Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction** and India's **National Disaster Management Plan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Features of the ICR-ER:**

 
 
• **Real-Time Surveillance:** The platform uses drones, CCTV, and satellite data to monitor disaster-hit areas.
 
• **Predictive Analytics:** Advanced AI tools predict potential disasters like floods or earthquakes based on historical data and environmental indicators.
 
• **GIS Mapping:** Geographical Information Systems are used to map affected areas and optimize resource allocation.
 
• **Mobile Connectivity:** The system ensures communication through mobile apps for citizens and disaster management teams.
 
 
 
• **Disaster Management Framework in India:**
 
 
• The **Disaster Management Act, 2005** provides the legal framework for disaster management in India.
 
• The **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)** is the apex body responsible for planning and coordinating disaster response.
 
• State Disaster Management Authorities (SDMAs) and District Disaster Management Authorities (DDMAs) implement measures at local levels.
 
• India follows the **Sendai Framework (2015-2030)**, focusing on disaster risk reduction and building resilience.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Advanced Disaster Management Platforms:**
 
 
• **USA:** Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) uses centralized command centers for disaster response.
 
• **Japan:** Advanced earthquake early warning systems are integrated into disaster management platforms.
 
• **India:** The ICR-ER is a significant step toward leveraging technology for disaster preparedness and response.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• The ICR-ER aligns with India's commitment to achieving the **UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly Goal 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities) and Goal 13 (Climate Action).
 
• The platform is designed to be scalable and adaptable, allowing for integration with **future technologies** and evolving disaster scenarios.
 
• India has faced significant disasters, including floods, cyclones, and earthquakes, highlighting the need for robust disaster management systems.
 
• In addition to ICR-ER, India has other initiatives like the **Indian Tsunami Early Warning System (ITEWS)** and **DAMS Safety Programme** to mitigate specific risks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Cotton Mission** has been planned for a duration of **5 years** as per the Union Budget 2025–26.
 
• The mission aims to enhance cotton productivity, especially in **extra-long staple varieties**, which are essential for high-quality textile production.
 
• This initiative seeks to support farmers by providing them with **advanced technology, better seeds, and improved farming practices**.
 
• The government will focus on promoting sustainable cotton cultivation methods to address challenges such as **soil degradation and water scarcity**.
 
• The Cotton Mission is expected to boost India's textile industry, which heavily relies on cotton, and strengthen its position as one of the leading exporters of cotton-based products globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Cotton in India:**

 
 
• India is the world's **largest producer of cotton**, contributing about 23% of global production.
 
• Cotton cultivation in India is primarily concentrated in states like **Maharashtra, Gujarat, Punjab, Haryana, and Tamil Nadu**.
 
• India has a rich diversity of cotton varieties, including both **short-staple and long-staple cotton**, catering to different industrial needs.
 
 
 
• **Extra-Long Staple Cotton:**
 
 
• Extra-long staple (ELS) cotton is known for its **high strength, superior quality, and durability**, making it ideal for premium textile products.
 
• India imports a significant quantity of ELS cotton due to **limited domestic production**.
 
• The Cotton Mission aims to reduce this dependency by increasing the production of ELS varieties domestically.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives to Support Cotton Farmers:**
 
 
• The **Technology Mission on Cotton** was launched earlier to improve cotton farming practices, ginning, and market accessibility.
 
• Subsidies on fertilizers, pesticides, and seeds are provided to cotton farmers under various schemes to **reduce input costs**.
 
• Programs like the **Minimum Support Price (MSP)** ensure fair pricing for farmers.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Textile Industry:**
 
 
• The Cotton Mission is expected to strengthen India's **textile exports**, which account for a significant portion of the country's foreign exchange earnings.
 
• It will also contribute to generating **employment opportunities** across the cotton value chain, from farming to textile manufacturing.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Challenges in Cotton Production:**

 
 
• Issues such as **pest attacks (e.g., bollworm)**, climate change, and water scarcity have significantly impacted cotton yields.
 
• Dependence on **imported seeds** for high-quality varieties has been a challenge for Indian farmers.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• Countries like **Egypt** and the **United States** are leaders in ELS cotton production, providing stiff competition to India.
 
• India's Cotton Mission aims to reduce this gap by improving **domestic production and quality**.
 
 
 
• **Technological Advancements:**
 
 
• Adoption of **genetically modified (GM) cotton** has significantly improved yields in India.
 
• Precision farming techniques, including **drip irrigation** and soil testing, are being promoted under the Cotton Mission.

questions.question: How many indigenously developed weapon systems were released by Defence Research and Development Organization (DRDO) in June 2024 to Indian armed forces under the emergency procurement clause?
questions.solution: The correct answer is __**28**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • **Defence Research and Development Organization (DRDO)** handed over **28 indigenously developed weapon systems** to the Indian Armed Forces in **June 2024** under the emergency procurement clause. • These weapon systems were designed and developed to meet the strategic needs of the **Indian Army, Navy, and Air Force**, focusing on enhancing their combat capabilities. • The emergency procurement clause allows for expedited acquisition of weapon systems, ensuring that the armed forces are equipped to handle immediate threats and operational requirements. • DRDO's initiative aligns with the **Make in India** policy, emphasizing self-reliance in defense production and reducing dependency on foreign imports. • These systems include advanced technologies such as **missiles, electronic warfare systems, radars, and communication systems**, catering to diverse operational needs.
